HiddenSize multiple-of-16 static_assert bounds complete vector blocks; H256 fits. No new public API or layout change.

checks.name: Clamp and signed zero
checks.reason: max(input,+0) then min(result,+1) has the same operand ordering as existing AVX2/SSE. The x86 max equal-zero result comes from the second operand, converting -0 to +0 exactly as existing vector paths do. Multiplication association is (a*a)*w and (b*b)*w, then term addition. Scalar clamp may retain -0 before squaring, which removes its sign before multiplication. No claim for NaNs or nondefault floating-point control modes.

checks.name: Sixteen partial sums and final reduction
checks.reason: One __m512 sum starts at +0; lane j processes h=j,j+16,... in increasing order. Per hidden unit, square, weight multiply, paired-term add, and sum add are separate. Final loop starts at *b2 and adds lanes0..15 in order. Existing evaluate-only.s independently inspected: clamp/multiply/add sequence plus sixteen scalar reduction additions. Centipawn multiplication/division, clamp, and int conversion are shared unchanged.
